Name: Tai Kwun Centre for Heritage and Arts
Location: 10 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Heritage centre in the former Central Police Station with several independent shops: TASCHEN (books, 11:00-19:00), LockCha Tea Shop (tea and Yixing teaware, 11:00-19:00), Bonart (botanical art), and Yuen's Tailor (bespoke, founded 1977). Why: The most complete colonial-era law-and-order compound in the city, free to wander, with Hollywood Road and SoHo restaurants at its doorstep. Good for architecture and history fans and anyone wanting a rainy-day or evening anchor.

Name: Hong Kong Palace Museum
Location: 8 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Museum of Chinese imperial art with loans from Beijing's Palace Museum, in a building by Rocco Design Architects inspired by traditional Chinese forms, set on the West Kowloon harbourfront. Why: Rare chance to see Forbidden City treasures in Hong Kong; combines culture with the WKCD waterfront.

Name: M+
Location: 38 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Herzog & de Meuron-designed museum of 20th and 21st century visual culture covering design, architecture, moving image and art, with a LED-facade towards the harbour. Why: Asia's flagship visual-culture museum; the building, harbour skyline views from the terrace and the Friday late opening make it a design pick. Current special exhibition is Design Ah! (to 10 Jan 2027).

Name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
Location: 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The government's art museum on the TST waterfront, reopened in 2019, with Chinese painting and calligraphy, Cantonese export art and local art shows. Why: Cheap, central and open until 21:00 on holidays, so a good Christmas evening culture stop; current shows include a Cantonese export art collection and Hong Kong at the Venice Biennale.

Name: Mei Ho House (Museum of Public Housing)
Location: Block 41, Shek Kip Mei Estate, Berwick Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A surviving 1954 H-shaped Mark I resettlement block, restored as a youth hostel with a free heritage museum on early public housing life. Why: Tells the story of the 1953 Shek Kip Mei fire and how HK public housing began; ideal for retro and social-history fans, and pairs with Sham Shui Po food and fabric streets.

Name: Chi Lin Nunnery and Nan Lian Garden
Location: 5 Chi Lin Drive, Diamond Hill, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A Tang-dynasty-style timber Buddhist nunnery beside a classical Chinese garden with ponds, rockeries and a red wooden bridge, both free to enter. Why: The best place in the city for traditional Chinese architecture and calm; ideal for architecture and photography fans, and close to Wong Tai Sin.

Name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
Location: 2 Chuk Yuen Village, Wong Tai Sin, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's most popular Taoist temple, with bright red-and-gold halls, a fortune-telling arcade and gardens, dedicated to the healing deity Wong Tai Sin. Why: Living religious practice (kau cim fortune sticks) on a grand scale; for culture lovers and fortune-seekers, with Chi Lin nearby.

Name: Man Mo Temple
Location: 124-126 Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 19th-century Taoist temple dedicated to the gods of literature and war, filled with huge hanging incense coils. Why: Atmospheric incense-smoke interiors in the middle of Hollywood Road antique shops; best for photographers and history fans.

Name: Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery
Location: Pai Tau Village, Sha Tin, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A hillside monastery reached by about 400 steps lined with golden Buddha statues, with a hall holding thousands of small Buddhas. Why: Quirky and uncommercial; good for those who like unusual religious art.

Name: Po Lin Monastery and Tian Tan Buddha
Location: Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A monastery with the 34-metre bronze Big Buddha on a hilltop, reached by the Ngong Ping 360 cable car or bus. Why: Hong Kong's best-known outdoor religious landmark; the cable car adds scenic views.

Name: Viva Blue House and Hong Kong House of Stories
Location: 72A Stone Nullah Lane, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 1920s-50s tong lau cluster (Blue, Yellow, Orange houses) still home to residents, with a small museum and free guided tours. Why: UNESCO-awarded conservation of a living tenement; ideal for retro and architecture fans.

Name: Lui Seng Chun
Location: 119 Lai Chi Kok Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 1931 corner tong lau with a mix of Chinese and Western design, now an HKBU Chinese medicine clinic and heritage centre. Why: One of the best-preserved tong lau in Kowloon.

Name: Former North Kowloon Magistracy (NK Future)
Location: Tonkin Street West, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 1960 Grade 2 historic building, former art college site, being turned into a judicial education centre called NK Future. Why: SCAD Hong Kong no longer operates there, as its lease ended in July 2020.

Name: Hong Kong Museum of History
Location: 100 Chatham Road South, Tsim Sha Tsui East, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Permanent Hong Kong Story exhibition reopened 1 April 2026 after a renovation begun in 2020, now on the ground floor only. Why: The main local-history museum; media dispute the revised content.

Name: Lei Cheng Uk Han Tomb Museum
Location: 41 Tonkin Street, Cheung Sha Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A brick tomb from the Eastern Han period preserved in a small museum. Why: Hong Kong's oldest dated structure; free.

Name: Hong Kong Maritime Museum
Location: Central Pier 8, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Museum on the Central waterfront. Why: Open 10:00-19:00 on Sat, Sun and public holidays, closed only on CNY days 1-2.

Name: Kai Tak Sports Park
Location: Kai Tak, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Populous-designed 28-hectare complex with a retractable-roof stadium, opened March 2025. Why: Modern landmark; event days make crowds.

Name: Peak Tram and Peak Tower
Location: Lower Terminus, 33 Garden Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The 1888 funicular up to Victoria Peak, with the Sky Terrace 428 viewing deck at the top. Why: The classic harbour view; queues are long on holidays, so go early or at dusk.
